# Try here first; production rate limits are far lower. Staging
# certificates are not trusted by browsers.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt-staging
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    # No email: ACME accounts need no contact, and Let's Encrypt sends
    # no expiry emails since 2025. Setting spec.acme.email later updates
    # the registered account.
    # Account key, created by cert-manager in its own namespace.
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-staging-account-key
    solvers:
      # HTTP-01 through Traefik's Ingress support; needs no Gateway, and
      # also answers for names served by Gateway listeners. The name
      # must reach port 80 of the cluster from the internet.
      - http01:
          ingress:
            ingressClassName: traefik
---
# Trusted certificates; same settings as staging.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-account-key
    solvers:
      - http01:
          ingress:
            ingressClassName: traefik

metadata.description: Serves Gateway API and Ingress, and hosts the CrowdSec bouncer. Ingress NGINX was retired in March 2026.

releases.name: traefik

profiles.multi-node:
deployment:
  # One pod per node, so every node keeps client addresses under the
  # Local traffic policy; k3s ServiceLB source-NATs on nodes without one.
  # From a Deployment, annotate it helm.sh/resource-policy=keep before the
  # upgrade and delete it after, or ingress drops for a few seconds.
  kind: DaemonSet
tolerations:
  # The taints k3s ServiceLB tolerates, so Traefik runs wherever it listens.
  - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
    operator: Exists
    effect: NoSchedule
  - key: CriticalAddonsOnly
    operator: Exists
metrics:
  prometheus:
    # Request rate and latency metrics.
    service:
      enabled: true
resources:
  # Headroom for higher request rates.
  requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
  limits: {memory: 512Mi}
profiles.single-node:
deployment:
  # A second copy gains nothing on one node.
  replicas: 1
resources:
  # Idles near 40Mi; the limit contains leaks.
  requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
  limits: {memory: 256Mi}

# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: traefik
  tag: v3.7.16@sha256:c8a121e4bb1347e8fd52657fab12f2cb70b68f8a018895e2068f92c9e519b9c2
providers:
  kubernetesGateway:
    # Route web services with HTTPRoute.
    enabled: true
  kubernetesIngress:
    # Many charts still ship Ingress objects.
    enabled: true
  kubernetesCRD:
    # Middleware objects, such as the CrowdSec bouncer.
    enabled: true
    # No references to other namespaces.
    allowCrossNamespace: false
    # Only the traefik namespace can set the default TLS store.
    defaultTLSResourcesNamespace: traefik
gatewayClass:
  # Gateways reference GatewayClass "traefik".
  enabled: true
  name: traefik
gateway:
  # Gateways and listeners are created per domain, not by the chart.
  enabled: false
api:
  # Unauthenticated surface; not needed.
  dashboard: false
service:
  spec:
    # Skip source NAT so Traefik sees client addresses (CrowdSec, rate
    # limits, logs); only nodes running Traefik serve traffic.
    externalTrafficPolicy: Local
accessLog:
  # JSON access logs for metrics, log search and CrowdSec.
  enabled: true
  format: json
  fields:
    # Keep only the fields below; secrets live in headers and queries.
    defaultMode: drop
    names:
      ClientHost: keep
      RequestHost: keep
      RequestMethod: keep
      RequestPath: keep
      RequestProtocol: keep
      DownstreamStatus: keep
      DownstreamContentSize: keep
      RequestContentSize: keep
      Duration: keep
      RouterName: keep
      StartUTC: keep
    headers:
      # Headers carry cookies and bearer tokens.
      defaultMode: drop
    queryParameters:
      # Query strings carry OAuth codes and signed-URL secrets.
      defaultMode: drop

risks.risk: A tenant HTTPRoute can claim another tenant's hostname on a shared listener.

metadata.description: Blocks brute-force attempts and scanners that show up in Traefik's access logs, for every app behind the ingress. It fails open, and the online API is off by default.
metadata.name: CrowdSec

releases.name: crowdsec
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: crowdsecurity/crowdsec
  tag: v1.8.1@sha256:0f2523fa61ef507f15d953045cface490cc880670c62f2755ced17524107f71a
# The runtime on k3s and mainstream distributions.
container_runtime: containerd
secrets:
  externalSecret:
    # Inputs, not chart-generated, so every render is identical.
    name: crowdsec-lapi
agent:
  acquisition:
    # Traefik's JSON access log.
    - namespace: traefik
      podName: traefik-*
      program: traefik
  env:
    # Parsers and scenarios for Traefik plus generic HTTP attacks.
    - name: COLLECTIONS
      value: crowdsecurity/traefik
lapi:
  env:
    # No data leaves the cluster unless the user opts in.
    - name: DISABLE_ONLINE_API
      value: "true"
    # Registers the Traefik bouncer (input bouncer-key).
    - name: BOUNCER_KEY_traefik
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef: {name: crowdsec-bouncer-key, key: key}
  persistentVolume:
    data:
      # SQLite decisions and bouncer registrations.
      enabled: true
    config:
      # Keeps machine credentials stable across restarts.
      enabled: true

releases.manifests:
# Referenced from Traefik's entrypoints as crowdsec-bouncer@kubernetescrd.
apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
kind: Middleware
metadata:
  name: bouncer
  namespace: crowdsec
spec:
  plugin:
    crowdsec-bouncer:
      enabled: true
      # Local copy of decisions; requests never wait on LAPI.
      crowdsecMode: stream
      crowdsecLapiScheme: http
      crowdsecLapiHost: crowdsec-service.crowdsec.svc.cluster.local:8080
      # Read from the Secret in the Middleware's namespace.
      crowdsecLapiKey: urn:k8s:secret:crowdsec-bouncer-key:key
      # Fail open: if LAPI is unreachable, keep serving traffic.
      updateMaxFailure: -1
releases.name: bouncer-middleware

risks.mitigation: Only administrators manage decisions. Configure trusted proxies before running CrowdSec behind a CDN.
risks.risk: A ban on a shared IP (NAT, CDN) blocks it for every tenant.

metadata.description: Keeps and searches log history with low memory and disk use. It is Apache-2.0, unlike Loki, and runs on the VictoriaMetrics operator.
metadata.name: VictoriaLogs

releases.manifests:
# The log store.
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1
kind: VLSingle
metadata:
  name: victoria-logs
  namespace: observability
spec:
  # Two weeks, or less when the volume reaches 8GiB of its 10Gi.
  retentionPeriod: 14d
  retentionMaxDiskSpaceUsageBytes: 8GiB
  storage:
    resources:
      requests: {storage: 10Gi}
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
    limits: {memory: 1Gi}
---
# One collector per node, reading container logs.
apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1
kind: VLAgent
metadata:
  name: collector
  namespace: observability
spec:
  k8sCollector:
    enabled: true
    # Namespace, pod and container suffice; labels add cardinality.
    includePodLabels: false
  remoteWrite:
    - url: http://vlsingle-victoria-logs.observability.svc:9428/internal/insert
  resources:
    requests: {cpu: 20m, memory: 32Mi}
    limits: {memory: 256Mi}
---
# Only the collector, the metrics stack's vmagent (the operator's scrape of
# /metrics) and Zeabur Proxy in the zeabur namespace reach the log store.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: victoria-logs
  namespace: observability
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vlsingle, app.kubernetes.io/instance: victoria-logs}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - ports: [{port: 9428, protocol: TCP}]
      from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vlagent, app.kubernetes.io/instance: collector}
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmagent}
        # Both selectors: anyone can label a pod in their own namespace.
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: zeabur}
          podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: zeabur-proxy}
releases.name: logs

risks.mitigation: A NetworkPolicy lets only the collector, vmagent and Zeabur Proxy reach it; tenants query through Zeabur Proxy, which filters by namespace.
risks.risk: The log store holds every tenant's logs in one place.

risks.mitigation: VictoriaLogs drops a line whose stream fields repeat, so it never lands under another namespace; re-run Zeabur Proxy's canary test on upgrades.
risks.risk: The collector adds a pod's JSON log fields to the line, so a pod can print kubernetes.pod_namespace to pose as another namespace.

security.summary: The collector reads pod metadata and node log files.

            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              buildrun: [metadata, name]
              build: [spec, buildRef]

              reason: [status, reason]

          - groupVersionKind: {group: postgresql.cnpg.io, version: v1, kind: Cluster}

          - groupVersionKind: {group: postgresql.cnpg.io, version: v1, kind: Backup}
            metricNamePrefix: zeabur_cnpg_backup
            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              backup: [metadata, name]
              cluster: [spec, cluster, name]
              phase: [status, phase]
            metrics:
              - name: created
                help: When the Backup was created, by its phase.
                each:
                  type: Gauge
                  gauge: {path: [metadata, creationTimestamp]}
          - groupVersionKind: {group: psmdb.percona.com, version: v1, kind: PerconaServerMongoDB}
            metricNamePrefix: zeabur_psmdb
            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              cluster: [metadata, name]
            metrics:
              - name: state
                help: The MongoDB cluster's state.
                each:
                  type: Info
                  info:
                    labelsFromPath:
                      state: [status, state]
          - groupVersionKind: {group: psmdb.percona.com, version: v1, kind: PerconaServerMongoDBBackup}
            metricNamePrefix: zeabur_psmdb_backup
            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              backup: [metadata, name]
              cluster: [spec, clusterName]
              state: [status, state]
            metrics:
              - name: created
                help: When the backup was created, by its state.
                each:
                  type: Gauge
                  gauge: {path: [metadata, creationTimestamp]}
          - groupVersionKind: {group: k8up.io, version: v1, kind: Backup}
            metricNamePrefix: zeabur_k8up_backup
            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              backup: [metadata, name]
            metrics:
              - name: condition_time
                help: When each condition of the Backup last changed, by type and reason.
                each:
                  type: Gauge
                  gauge:
                    path: [status, conditions]
                    labelsFromPath:
                      type: [type]
                      reason: [reason]
                    valueFrom: [lastTransitionTime]
          - groupVersionKind: {group: velero.io, version: v1, kind: Backup}
            metricNamePrefix: zeabur_velero_backup
            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              backup: [metadata, name]
              phase: [status, phase]
            metrics:
              - name: created
                help: When the Velero backup was created, by its phase.
                each:
                  type: Gauge
                  gauge: {path: [metadata, creationTimestamp]}
          - groupVersionKind: {group: cert-manager.io, version: v1, kind: Certificate}
            metricNamePrefix: zeabur_certmanager_certificate
            labelsFromPath:
              namespace: [metadata, namespace]
              certificate: [metadata, name]
            metrics:
              - name: not_after
                help: When the issued certificate expires.
                errorLogV: 5
                each:
                  type: Gauge
                  gauge: {path: [status, notAfter]}
              - name: condition
                help: The Certificate's conditions, 1 when true.
                each:
                  type: Gauge
                  gauge:
                    path: [status, conditions]
                    labelsFromPath:
                      type: [type]
                    valueFrom: [status]
  vmScrape:
    spec:
      endpoints:
        # The chart's endpoint, plus two drops. The rules read failed
        # backups only. Each successful backup adds one series.
        - port: http
          honorLabels: true
          metricRelabelConfigs:
            - action: labeldrop
              regex: (uid|container_id|image_id)
            - action: drop
              if: '{__name__="zeabur_cnpg_backup_created", phase="completed"}'
            - action: drop
              if: '{__name__="zeabur_psmdb_backup_created", state="ready"}'
alertmanager:
  spec:
    # Each project keeps its channels in VMAlertmanagerConfigs. The operator
    # then routes a config only its own namespace's alerts, and refuses one
    # that reads files from the Alertmanager pod.
    disableNamespaceMatcher: false
    arbitraryFSAccessThroughSMs:
      deny: true

  spec:
    # 30s cuts scrape cost by a third versus the chart's 20s.
    scrapeInterval: 30s

apiVersion: operator.victoriametrics.com/v1beta1
kind: VMRule
metadata:
  name: zeabur-notifications
  namespace: observability
spec:
  groups:
    - name: zeabur-project
      interval: 30s
      rules:
        - alert: ZeaburBuildFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, build, buildrun, reason) (
              zeabur_builder_buildrun_completion_time{phase="Failed"}
            ) > time() - 900
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: build-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Build {{ $labels.build }} failed ({{ $labels.reason }})."
            description: "BuildRun {{ $labels.buildrun }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed with reason {{ $labels.reason }}."
        - alert: ZeaburBuildSucceeded
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, build, buildrun) (
              zeabur_builder_buildrun_completion_time{phase="Succeeded"}
            ) > time() - 900
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: build-succeeded, zeabur_kind: event, severity: info}
          annotations:
            summary: "Build {{ $labels.build }} succeeded."
            description: "BuildRun {{ $labels.buildrun }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} succeeded."
        # The Deployment controller gives up on a rollout after
        # progressDeadlineSeconds (600 by default).
        - alert: ZeaburDeployFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, deployment) (
              kube_deployment_status_condition{condition="Progressing", status="false"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: deploy-failed, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Deployment of {{ $labels.deployment }} failed."
            description: "The rollout of {{ $labels.deployment }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} passed its progress deadline."
        # A rollout makes a new ReplicaSet. It succeeded when the
        # Deployment then runs only up-to-date, available replicas. A
        # rollback to an earlier ReplicaSet does not count.
        - alert: ZeaburDeploySucceeded
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, deployment) (
              label_replace(
                (time() - kube_replicaset_created < 1800)
                * on (namespace, replicaset) group_left (owner_name)
                kube_replicaset_owner{owner_kind="Deployment"},
                "deployment", "$1", "owner_name", "(.+)"
              )
            )
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_observed_generation == kube_deployment_metadata_generation)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_updated == kube_deployment_spec_replicas)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available == kube_deployment_spec_replicas)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas == kube_deployment_spec_replicas)
            and on (namespace, deployment) (kube_deployment_spec_replicas > 0)
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: deploy-succeeded, zeabur_kind: event, severity: info}
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.deployment }} is deployed."
            description: "All replicas of {{ $labels.deployment }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} run the new version."
        - alert: ZeaburCrashLooping
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, pod, container) (
              kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason="CrashLoopBackOff"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 5m
          labels: {zeabur_event: crash-loop, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.pod }} keeps crashing."
            description: "Container {{ $labels.container }} of {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has been in CrashLoopBackOff for 5 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburOutOfMemory
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, pod, container) (
              kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace, pod, container) (
              max by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[10m])) > 0
            )
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: out-of-memory, zeabur_kind: event, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "{{ $labels.pod }} ran out of memory."
            description: "Container {{ $labels.container }} of {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} used its memory limit and restarted."
        # Without the phase in the grouping, a move from one unhealthy
        # phase to another does not restart the 15 minutes.
        - alert: ZeaburPostgresUnhealthy
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster) (
              zeabur_cnpg_cluster_phase{phase!="Cluster in healthy state"}
            ) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 15m
          labels: {zeabur_event: database-unhealthy, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "PostgreSQL {{ $labels.cluster }} is not healthy."
            description: "PostgreSQL cluster {{ $labels.cluster }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has not been healthy for 15 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburMongoDBUnhealthy
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster) (zeabur_psmdb_state{state="error"}) == 1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: database-unhealthy, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "MongoDB {{ $labels.cluster }} is in error."
            description: "MongoDB cluster {{ $labels.cluster }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has been in error for 10 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburPostgresBackupFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster, backup) (
              zeabur_cnpg_backup_created{phase=~"failed|walArchivingFailing"}
            ) > time() - 21600
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} of PostgreSQL {{ $labels.cluster }} failed."
            description: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
        - alert: ZeaburMongoDBBackupFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, cluster, backup) (
              zeabur_psmdb_backup_created{state=~"error|rejected"}
            ) > time() - 21600
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} of MongoDB {{ $labels.cluster }} failed."
            description: "Backup {{ $labels.backup }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
        - alert: ZeaburVolumeBackupFailed
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, backup) (
              zeabur_k8up_backup_condition_time{type="Completed", reason="Failed"}
            ) > time() - 21600
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Volume backup {{ $labels.backup }} failed."
            description: "K8up backup {{ $labels.backup }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} failed."
        # Volumes on local-path report no usage; this covers the others.
        - alert: ZeaburVolumeAlmostFull
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (
              kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes
            ) < 0.1
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: volume-almost-full, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} is almost full."
            description: "Less than 10% of volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} is free."
        # cert-manager renews 30 days before expiry, so 14 days left
        # means renewal keeps failing.
        - alert: ZeaburCertificateExpiring
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, certificate) (zeabur_certmanager_certificate_not_after) - time() < 14 * 86400
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          labels: {zeabur_event: certificate, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} expires soon."
            description: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} expires in less than 14 days and was not renewed."
        - alert: ZeaburCertificateNotReady
          expr: |
            max by (namespace, certificate) (zeabur_certmanager_certificate_condition{type="Ready"}) == 0
            and on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""}
          for: 1h
          labels: {zeabur_event: certificate, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} is not ready."
            description: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} in {{ $labels.namespace }} has not been issued for an hour."
        # Zeabur creates a short-lived Job with this label to test a
        # channel. The namespace comes from the Job, so a person can
        # only test the channels of a namespace where they create Jobs.
        - alert: ZeaburNotificationTest
          expr: |
            label_replace(
              max by (namespace, label_zeabur_com_notification_test) (
                kube_job_labels{label_zeabur_com_notification_test!=""}
              ),
              "zeabur_channel", "$1", "label_zeabur_com_notification_test", "(.+)"
            )
          labels: {zeabur_event: test, zeabur_kind: event, severity: info}
          annotations:
            summary: "Test notification from Zeabur."
            description: "This channel receives notifications from {{ $labels.namespace }}."
    - name: zeabur-cluster
      interval: 30s
      # The cluster's channels are in observability.
      labels: {namespace: observability}
      rules:
        - alert: ZeaburNodeNotReady
          expr: |
            max by (node) (kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready", status="true"}) == 0
          for: 5m
          labels: {zeabur_event: node-not-ready, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Node {{ $labels.node }} is not ready."
            description: "Node {{ $labels.node }} has not been ready for 5 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburNodeDiskAlmostFull
          expr: |
            max by (instance, mountpoint) (
              node_filesystem_avail_bytes{fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs"}
            ) < 0.1
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: volume-almost-full, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Disk {{ $labels.mountpoint }} on {{ $labels.instance }} is almost full."
            description: "Less than 10% of {{ $labels.mountpoint }} on {{ $labels.instance }} is free."
        - alert: ZeaburSystemCrashLooping
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, pod, container) (
                kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason="CrashLoopBackOff"}
              ) == 1
              unless on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""},
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          for: 5m
          labels: {zeabur_event: crash-loop, zeabur_kind: state, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "System pod {{ $labels.pod }} keeps crashing."
            description: "Container {{ $labels.container }} of {{ $labels.pod }} in {{ $labels.object_namespace }} has been in CrashLoopBackOff for 5 minutes."
        - alert: ZeaburSystemVolumeAlmostFull
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (
                kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes / kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes
              ) < 0.1
              unless on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""},
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          for: 10m
          labels: {zeabur_event: volume-almost-full, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} is almost full."
            description: "Less than 10% of volume {{ $labels.persistentvolumeclaim }} in {{ $labels.object_namespace }} is free."
        - alert: ZeaburSystemCertificateExpiring
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, certificate) (zeabur_certmanager_certificate_not_after) - time() < 14 * 86400
              unless on (namespace) kube_namespace_labels{label_zeabur_com_project!=""},
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          labels: {zeabur_event: certificate, zeabur_kind: state, severity: warning}
          annotations:
            summary: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} expires soon."
            description: "Certificate {{ $labels.certificate }} in {{ $labels.object_namespace }} expires in less than 14 days and was not renewed."
        - alert: ZeaburClusterBackupFailed
          expr: |
            label_move(
              max by (namespace, backup) (
                zeabur_velero_backup_created{phase=~"Failed|PartiallyFailed|FailedValidation"}
              ) > time() - 21600,
              "namespace", "object_namespace"
            )
          labels: {zeabur_event: backup-failed, zeabur_kind: event, severity: critical}
          annotations:
            summary: "Cluster backup {{ $labels.backup }} failed."
            description: "Velero backup {{ $labels.backup }} did not complete."

spec:

    - from:

            matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: falco}

        - {port: 9093, protocol: TCP}

        - {port: 9093, protocol: TCP}
        - {port: 8435, protocol: TCP}

    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: vmalertmanager}
      ports:
        - {port: 9094, protocol: TCP}
        - {port: 9094, protocol: UDP}

metadata.description: Block storage replicated across nodes: a volume survives losing its node, follows its pod to another node, and can be expanded in place. Recommended on multi-node, where it becomes the default storage class. Optional on single-node, where a replica has nowhere else to go; it still gives expandable volumes and snapshots there.
metadata.name: Longhorn

releases.name: longhorn

profiles.multi-node:
persistence:
  # New volumes without a class survive losing a node. local-path stays
  # available for databases that replicate themselves.
  defaultClass: true
defaultSettings:
  # A pod on a dead node otherwise holds its volume until someone
  # force-deletes it; this lets it start elsewhere.
  nodeDownPodDeletionPolicy: delete-both-statefulset-and-deployment-pod
profiles.single-node:
persistence:
  # local-path stays the default: on one node it is faster, and
  # Longhorn is for volumes that need to grow.
  defaultClass: false
  # One node: a second replica would sit on the same disk.
  defaultClassReplicaCount: 1
csi:
  # One node: the chart's three replicas of each sidecar gain nothing.
  attacherReplicaCount: 1
  provisionerReplicaCount: 1
  resizerReplicaCount: 1
  snapshotterReplicaCount: 1
longhornGlobalManager:
  # One node: the chart's three warm standbys gain nothing.
  replicas: 1

releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  longhorn:
    manager:
      repository: longhornio/longhorn-manager
      tag: v1.13.0@sha256:7372f3c59239e9a67c0017b3af32fabdf08c4dcc0631140161da9a47e3b142f0

      tag: v1.13.0@sha256:f22fb0254ae50195c1635ce428dfae26375956b3d7bd39640fae8fe33a236023
persistence:
  # One copy per node, up to three: losing a node leaves two while the
  # third rebuilds. Two nodes give two copies; with one down, volumes
  # run on a single copy until it is back.
  defaultClassReplicaCount: 3
  # Volumes outlive their claims only when a person asks for it, as with local-path.
  reclaimPolicy: Delete
defaultSettings:
  # With fewer nodes than replicas, volumes still attach (degraded) and gain
  # their missing replicas as nodes join, so a class asking for 3 gives
  # min(3, nodes) copies.
  allowVolumeCreationWithDegradedAvailability: true
  # Spread existing replicas onto nodes that join later.
  replicaAutoBalance: best-effort
  # No calls to Longhorn's upgrade server; versions change with the catalog.
  upgradeChecker: false
  allowCollectingLonghornUsageMetrics: false
  # After a Longhorn upgrade, move attached volumes to the new engine one
  # node at a time; otherwise they stay on the old one until done by hand.
  concurrentAutomaticEngineUpgradePerNodeLimit: 1

  # default, no Ingress); reach it with kubectl port-forward.
  replicas: 1

metadata.description: Backs up the whole cluster to S3 for disaster recovery. It can touch any namespace, so it is for administrators only.
metadata.name: Velero

releases.name: velero
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: docker.io/velero/velero
  tag: v1.18.2@sha256:37396519f399536e5f01427d723565ae69294ec3fb5625cf1c87c09eaa9de16b
initContainers:
  # AWS plugin covers any S3-compatible store; v1.14.x matches Velero 1.18.
  - name: velero-plugin-for-aws
    image: velero/velero-plugin-for-aws:v1.14.4@sha256:c85a7fa803569e3128c33e4f5766f84ab156c8d171c9f1dd2715581d45ce98fa
    volumeMounts:
      - mountPath: /target
        name: plugins
credentials:
  # Secret comes from the credentials input, not the chart.
  useSecret: true
  existingSecret: velero-credentials
configuration:
  backupStorageLocation:
    # One S3 location; bucket and URL are inputs.
    - name: default
      provider: aws
      default: true
      config:
        region: us-east-1
        s3ForcePathStyle: "true"
        # Velero writes Secrets into the backup as they are. The
        # store encrypts them with the backup-key input (SSE-C).
        customerKeyEncryptionSecret: velero-backup-key/key
  # Kopia file-system backups work on any storage class, local-path included.
  uploaderType: kopia
  # No node agent by default, so no volume copy. Backups opt in with file-backup.
  defaultVolumesToFsBackup: false
# CSI snapshots need per-driver setup; use file-system backups instead.
snapshotsEnabled: false

security.credentialsNote: Needs static S3 credentials. All backups share one Kopia password and one SSE-C key, both in Secrets in the velero namespace.

risks.mitigation: Never grant Velero CRDs to tenants.
risks.risk: Backups and Restores can include any namespace, including other tenants' Secrets.

risks.mitigation: Take one backup by hand after install, then download backups/<name>/velero-backup.json without the key: the store must refuse it. SeaweedFS supports SSE-C.
risks.risk: SSE-C sends the key with each request, so the S3 server sees the backup before it encrypts it. A store without SSE-C refuses the uploads, or ignores the key and keeps the backups in clear text.

risks.mitigation: Keep a copy of both Secrets outside the cluster. Before a restore into a new cluster, create them first.
risks.risk: Without the velero-repo-credentials and velero-backup-key Secrets, nobody can read the backups. Both are also inside the backups that they encrypt.

security.summary: Bound to cluster-admin; reads and restores every object. By default no Pod is privileged and the velero namespace needs only the baseline Pod Security level. With the file-backup input, a root node agent on every node holds the same token, mounts host paths and needs the privileged level.

upgradeNotes.note: Upgrade the AWS plugin together with Velero.

If Velero ran before velero-repo-credentials existed, Velero made it with its public default password, and Kopia keeps the password of a repository. Point the location at a new prefix to start encrypted repositories. Backups made before SSE-C stay unencrypted.
